purpose: Teach: 激突/宝庫/博し/中澤/中尾/江原/大原/大川

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、車両激突事故の交通工学研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on traffic engineering research into vehicle collision accidents, didn't you?
lines.style: Steady, observant tone. Gentle confirmation rather than question. Slight pause before his name—she's gathering her thoughts. Not checking a list; engaging with genuine interest in his work.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、京都の文化財の宝庫、つまり史料庫の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I actually wrote my paper on research into Kyoto's cultural heritage archives.
lines.style: Quiet but clear correction. A small, careful breath before the pivot. He's not defensive, just precise—setting the record straight with the gentleness of someone used to being misunderstood.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、芸能界で人気を博した役者の社会学研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on sociological research into actors who became popular in entertainment, didn't you?
lines.style: Same steady warmth as before. A slight note of curiosity—she's testing whether he'll correct her again, or perhaps she's genuinely uncertain. The rhythm is unhurried.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、報道写真家中澤氏のドキュメンタリー研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I wrote my paper on documentary research focusing on photographer Nakazawa.
lines.style: Patient, unhurried correction. A soft clarity in his voice—he's used to this now. No frustration, just the quiet precision of someone who knows what he actually studied.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、政治学者中尾先生のご研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on research by political scientist Professor Nakao, didn't you?
lines.style: Her tone carries a warmth now—almost knowing. A beat before speaking, as if she's inviting him to complete the pattern. Still calm, but there's almost a gentle smile in her voice.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、霊能者江原氏の社会受容の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I wrote my paper on research into social reception of psychic Ehara.
lines.style: Clear and steady. His corrections have settled into a rhythm now. There's a kind of quiet confidence in his voice—he knows what he wrote, and he's not rattled by the questions.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、考古学者大原先生のご研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on research by archaeologist Professor Ohara, didn't you?
lines.style: The same gentle warmth as before. Her pacing is deliberate—she's watching him. There's almost a playfulness underneath, but it stays warm and respectful.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、報道写真家大川氏の社会写真の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I wrote my paper on research into documentary photography and social photography by photographer Okawa.
lines.style: His final answer. Clear and complete, with no hesitation now. A small sense of arrival—he's stated his case clearly. Warm underneath the precision, almost relieved.
